The total difficulty of cooling in space is vastly harder than on the ground

But 99.9999% of that challenge is Starship

Once you have the ability to get huge amounts of mass into space cheaply, it is genuinely easier to cool things in space

Your cooling system is passive

Just a giant piece of metal that is a) light w/ b) high thermal conductivity 

Aluminum is a good candidate

And then you have a working fluid that just circulates forever inside the metal structure
 
Ammonia is historical industry standard for radiators in space

You need a fluid where the critical point is optimized around the temperature of the chips

The working fluid goes from liquid phase to gas phase near the chips, and this change in density drives the hotter gas to pump heat through a loop

The high thermal conductivity of aluminum rips heat out of the fluid and black body radiation ejects heat into space

Black body radiation goes like temperature to the 4th power so the hotter you can run chips and hotter you can get the working fluid the better you can shed heat

It's honestly a way simpler system than on the ground

Eiji Aonuma says he decided to remake Ocarina of Time in part to help train the younger staff on future Zelda games:

"This year marks the 40th anniversary of the very first Legend of Zelda game. With that in mind, I was thinking about what I should create as the producer of the series. Many of the team members who work alongside me on Legend of Zelda games today have only experienced developing the more recent titles. That led me to wonder, 'Do they truly understand just how significant The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was to the series as a whole?' 

Of course, there are team members who vaguely know the game, and those who played it in their childhood days. But I started to wonder how they'd interpret The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as they go about developing future Legend of Zelda games. 

By learning the game structure and development style behind the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and by actually rebuilding it as a full remake, it may trigger new insights that they can carry forward into future development. If we could achieve that, I thought it would be incredibly valuable. That’s what led us to the conclusion that now is the right time to revisit The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time once again."
